title: Follow-up After Oncological Resection by Endoscopic Colorectal ESD (Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection)
official: Follow-up After Oncological Resection by Endoscopic Colorectal ESD
summary: Colorectal cancer is a common and leading cause of death. Pre-cancerous lesions, as well as some so-called superficial cancers, can be resected via endoscopy. The technique chosen in the case of extensive lesions or superficial cancer is submucosal dissection. This technique helps avoid surgery, which has a higher morbidity and mortality (especially due to the non-preservation of the organ).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adult patient (18 years or older).
* Presumed diagnosis of localized superficial colorectal cancer (T1) during endoscopy using the Conecct classification, confirmed by subsequent histopathological analysis.
* Patient included in the French Colorectal ESD Cohort in Experts Centers (FECCo registry) since September 2019 for submucosal dissection.
* Histological analysis of the resection specimen revealing a superficial colorectal adenocarcinoma with high risk of lymphatic recurrence, defined by at least one of the following criteria: submucosal invasion depth ≥ 1000 microns, tumor budding grade ≥ 2, presence of lymphatic and/or vascular emboli.

Exclusion Criteria:

* History of Crohn's disease (ICD-10: K50) or ulcerative colitis (ICD-10: K51).
* History of familial adenomatous polyposis and/or genetic predisposition to colorectal cancer (ICD-10: D12.6+0/1/2/4/5 and 6).
* Malignant tumor of the colon staged ≥ T2.
* Patients not included in the FECCo registry.
* Documented objection through the non-opposition form following review of the information notice
